Class PriceHistoryBackfill

java.lang.Object
com.leap.leaplaughlove.marketdata.history.PriceHistoryBackfill
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.boot.ApplicationRunner
@Component @ConditionalOnProperty(prefix="marketdata.history.backfill", name="enabled", havingValue="true", matchIfMissing=true) public class PriceHistoryBackfill extends Object implements org.springframework.boot.ApplicationRunner
Generates a synthetic price history for instruments that have none, so charts have something to draw before the live simulation has been running long enough to produce it. Without this, candle history only covers the current process's uptime and every range longer than that is empty.

One GBM path is walked per instrument at stepSeconds resolution across the whole lookback, and every configured bucket width is folded out of that single path. Deriving all widths from one walk is what keeps them consistent: the daily, hourly and minute series are aggregations of the same prices rather than independent random paths that would disagree about what the price was on a given afternoon. Only the finest width is stored at full resolution over a short window; wider widths cover proportionally longer ones, which is what makes a year of history cost thousands of rows per instrument instead of ~525,000.

Runs as an ApplicationRunner, which Spring Boot invokes before it publishes ApplicationReadyEvent. That ordering is deliberate and load-bearing: the backfill finishes before MarketSimulationEngine.initialize() reads the latest close, so the live feed resumes from the end of the generated history instead of jumping back to the seed price.

Idempotent per instrument - an instrument that already has any candle is left untouched, so this is a no-op on every boot after the first. Each instrument is written in its own transaction, so a failure part-way through cannot leave an instrument holding a truncated history that the idempotency check would then treat as complete.
